Ava S.: quick Q — I booked an award ticket using frequent flyer miles for an international trip, paid only $72 in taxes/fees. Can I expense the $72? Also curious how upgrades bought with cash or points are handled.
Devon (People Ops): short answer: yes, you can expense mandatory taxes/fees on award tickets. we treat the taxes/fees portion like a normal ticket fare for expense purposes. upgrades are a bit different — depends whether they're business-necessary or optional. :airplane:
Ava S.: great. what's required as proof? I only have the airline email showing miles redemption and a separate credit card charge for $72.
Devon (People Ops): please include: 1) the airline confirmation showing the award booking (itinerary + record locator), 2) the itemized receipt or credit card charge for the taxes/fees showing date and amount, and 3) if the award booking doesn’t show passenger name on the receipt, include the screenshot/email that links the charge to your booking. attach everything to the expense.
Marta (Finance): finance note: we need the itemized charge that shows the merchant and amount. a card statement line alone is acceptable only with the booking confirmation tying it to travel. for non-USD charges include the card exchange rate or statement converted amount.
Ava S.: what if I paid the taxes/fees on the corporate card?
Devon (People Ops): corporate card is fine and preferred. if Travel Desk booked the award taxes/fees on the corporate card, you don't need to file an expense. if you used your personal card, file as a travel expense with the receipts.
Ava S.: about upgrades  I used miles to upgrade one leg and paid $40 for an airport upgrade fee. Is that reimbursable?
Devon (People Ops): upgrades purchased purely for personal comfort are not reimbursable. exceptions: 1) if upgrade was required for a customer meeting (e.g., needed additional rest or extra seat for equipment) and preapproved by your manager and people-ops, or 2) if corporate policy or customer requires a minimum cabin for long-haul flights. for paid upgrade fees, include manager preapproval and a short justification.
Marta (Finance): additionally, if an upgrade results in materially higher out-of-pocket than an economy refundable ticket priced similarly, reviewers will ask for reasonableness.
Ava S.: and hotel loyalty points stays? I used points for two nights and paid resort fees and local taxes. expense those?
Devon (People Ops): same principle: mandatory taxes/mandatory resort fees tied to the stay are reimbursable. if the hotel posts a small incidental charge (mini-bar, movies) those are personal and not covered. submit the hotel folio showing nights, the points redemption line (if present), and the charges you paid.
TravelTeamBot: tip: when using award/points bookings, keep screenshots of the redemption confirmation and the payment receipt for taxes/fees. it makes expense review much faster.
Ava S.: any special coding in Concur/Expensify?
Devon (People Ops): use "Airfare - Award Ticket Taxes/Fees" for the airfare line. for upgraded legs use "Airfare - Upgrade (preapproved)" only if you have explicit approval. attach manager email in the expense.
Marta (Finance): one more thing: if the company-paid portion would have been cheaper had Travel Desk booked a revenue ticket, finance may request explanation. when in doubt, ask the Travel Desk before booking award taxes on your personal card.
Ava S.: thanks — i'll attach the confirmation + charge and submit. i'll ping my manager for preapproval on the upgrade leg in case we need it.
Devon (People Ops): perfect — if you want us to fast-track review, cc your manager on the expense or include the approval screenshot. thanks! :sparkles:
